D008_m001.question:
For the last month or so, it’s like I’ve been on some kind of rollercoaster I can’t get off. I’ll wake up feeling on top of the world, convinced I can take on ten cases at once. I’ve been emailing clients at 3 or 4 a.m., drafting motions, sketching out new business ideas, reorganizing the firm’s entire strategy — all at the same time. I barely sleep, maybe two or three hours, and I don’t even feel tired. It’s more that my mind just won’t shut up. Thoughts are racing so fast I can’t grab onto any one of them. I’ll start reading a brief, then jump to another file, then start planning a new practice area, and nothing actually gets finished. My staff says I’m snapping at them one minute and then overly enthusiastic the next. It’s starting to scare them, and honestly, it’s scaring me too.

Before this “high” stretch, I spent about two months in a really dark place. I could hardly get myself to the office. Even simple emails felt impossible. I was exhausted all the time, even when I slept a full night. I kept replaying old cases where I made minor errors, or the divorce, beating myself up over every misstep, convinced I’d ruined my life and career. Everything felt pointless, and I just couldn’t make myself care about work or anything else.
D008_m001.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

I guess this started about eight months ago. For around five months I was… weirdly “on.” At first it felt good, like I’d finally unlocked some hidden potential. I barely slept but I wasn’t tired; I was constantly sketching, pitching ideas to my boss, telling him I could handle whole chapters by myself, even my own series soon. I’d get annoyed so fast if anyone suggested I slow down or edited my work—I’d snap at my coworkers over tiny things. I couldn’t sit still, always pacing around the studio, double‑checking panels, starting new projects before finishing old ones. And I just wouldn’t shut up; my friends said hanging out with me was exhausting because I’d talk nonstop and jump from topic to topic.

Then it all sort of crashed. For the last three months, I cry over nothing, even random webtoons or ads. Things I used to dream about—like getting credited more or starting my own work—just feel pointless now. Food doesn’t appeal to me; I have to force myself to eat. I sleep long hours but wake up feeling heavy and drained. I’ve missed deadlines, avoided my team, and honestly don’t care, which scares me.
